html:
Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth and last human guru of the Sikhs. He led them from 1675 to 1708 and turned a community of believers into a people ready to fight.

He was born at Patna in 1666. When he was nine his father, Guru Tegh Bahadur, was beheaded in Delhi on the orders of Aurangzeb for refusing to convert to Islam. The boy grew up in the hills at Anandpur, trained in arms and learned in Persian, Sanskrit and Braj poetry.

In 1699 he called the Sikhs together and created the Khalsa, an order of the committed (see the founding of the Khalsa). Its members took a new initiation, the name Singh or Kaur, and five signs to wear, among them uncut hair and a sword. Caste was to count for nothing among them.

War with the hill kings and the Mughal governors followed. He lost all four sons: two died in battle at Chamkaur in 1704, and the two youngest, aged nine and six, were walled up alive at Sirhind. He wrote Aurangzeb a letter in Persian verse charging him with breaking his oath.

He was stabbed by an assassin and died at Nanded in 1708. Before he died he named the scripture, the Granth, as the Sikhs' guru for all time.
sum: Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth and last human guru of the Sikhs. He led them from 1675 to 1708 and turned a community of believers into a people ready to fight.
